page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.large is an arm64 compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features an AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processor operating at 2.6 GHz, providing 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. System memory is sized at 4.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The CPU cache architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, complemented by hardware AES cryptographic extensions. The server does not bundle local disk storage, relying on network-attached EBS volumes, and includes no discrete GPU hardware. Network connectivity delivers a baseline throughput of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations highlight steady single-core compute performance alongside predictable limits in multi-core scalability. In stress-ng testing, single-core execution reached 1532.89, while Geekbench single-core returned a score of 1514.0. Single-threaded data handling was consistent, with gzip compression achieving 24.09 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is bounded by the two available execution threads, resulting in a Geekbench multi-core rating of 2757.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 17.68 GB/sec. Memory subsystem bandwidth registered 57.94 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB read blocks and 20.86 GB/sec on large-block writes. Application workloads recorded Redis throughput of 3.43 million SET operations per second and static web serving speeds of 4.38 GB/sec.

The hardware profile delivers cost efficiency through modern ARM architecture and high network capability relative to its small CPU footprint. The primary tradeoff lies in the low memory capacity and the absence of integrated NVMe storage, making the instance unsuitable for large in-memory databases or parallel builds. The server is well matched for network-focused proxying, API routing, lightweight containerized microservices, and small-scale web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gn.large is a compute-optimized instance utilizing AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processors built on the Nitro System. Operating at 2.6 GHz across 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs with 1 thread per core, the instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, or 2.0 GB per core, adhering to a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. It provides a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps, includes hardware AES cryptographic support, and relies exclusively on remote EBS storage due to the absence of integrated local drives. Benchmark evaluations show balanced single-core execution with Geekbench single-core scores of 1514.0 and gzip compression at 24.09 GB/sec, while multi-core metrics reflect the physical dual-core limit. Given its combination of 6 Gbps networking, low memory footprint, and dedicated Graviton cores, the c7gn.large provides a cost-effective operational profile for network-sensitive edge services, reverse proxies, lightweight containerized microservices, and modest web-serving workloads.
